newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Best on Ground - Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules Column.
newsitem.headline: Best on Ground - Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules Column.

text.p: THE ENDLESS WINTER
If a week is a long time in football, then four months is an eternity.

After the opening round Collingwood led the table when it thrashed Port Adelaide, Richmond had a solid win over a Geelong team expected to miss the finals, the Western Bulldogs -- most people's pick for a bottom two finish -- lost to lowly Fremantle in Melbourne and grand finalists North Melbourne and Sydney were soundly beaten.

Sixteen rounds later Collingwood is languishing in 13th spot, the fledgling Port Adelaide looks like making the finals, Richmond is second last, Geelong is on top closely followed by the Western Bulldogs, Fremantle is competitive and North Melbourne and Sydney will again be thereabouts come September.
It should be no surprise, therefore, that Fremantle was the only team to repeat its first round result when the protaganists met again on the weekend.
The Dockers kept their finals hopes alive when they withstood a late burst by the Western Bulldogs to win by a goal in a spiteful match at Subiaco Oval on Sunday.
In warm conditions, the Dockers gained the early ascendancy, forcing the Bulldogs to play catch-up footy for the rest of the match.

Dockers' officials were fuming after rover Luke Toia left the ground in the opening minute with a badly swollen eye and Andrew Wills and Andrew McGovern finished the game with cuts to their faces and necks.

The Bulldogs cling to second place but their proud record of not having lost consecutive games all season was ruined. Indeed, a third consecutive loss looms when they play Sydney at the SCG this week.
SAINTS BEDEVIL HAWKS

St Kilda sent Hawthorn crashing out of the top eight and showed why it is a genuine premiership threat thrashing the Hawks by 79 points at Waverley Park on Saturday, its biggest ever win over its perrenial nemesis.
Led by the outstanding Robert Harvey who had 40 possessions and four opponents, the Saints set up their win in the third quarter with nine unanswered goals to lead by 79 points at the last change.
Harvey was given too much latitude by his first opponent Daniel Harford and the young Hawk was belatedly moved by Ken Judge in the third quarter and replaced with Chris Scott.
The final margin flattered the Hawks who have lost their past two games by an aggregate of 155 points and are looking decidedly mediocre.
Carlton kicked its highest score of the season and killed off Essendon's faint finals hopes with a 79 point thrashing at the MCG on Saturday.
The Blues celebrated Greg Williams' 250th game after half time with 14 goals to five to move to 10th on the ladder and stay in the finals' race.
Williams, in his last season, collected 29 possessions while ruckman Mark Porter, Justin Madden's replacement on the senior list, capped a great debut game with 27 hit-outs.
RILED PLUGGER IN WRESTLING REPORT
Sydney full-forward Tony Lockett was one of four players reported in the Swans' 37-point win over West Coast at the SCG on Saturday night.
Lockett's report for wrestling came in the first quarter when the Swans appeared unsettled and looked to be headed for their first home defeat in 18 matches.
The Eagles, without the injured Glen Jakovich, were weakened further by the late withdrawal of key defenders Ashley McIntosh and Guy McKenna.
McIntosh's absence left the Eagles a tall man short in defence and allowed Sydney centre half forward Stefan Carey to exert a strong influence on the game.
Ladder leader Geelong ended Richmond's final hopes and celebrated Gary Hocking's 200th game with a 32 point win at Kardinia Park on Saturday.
Geelong forward Derek Hall kept his team in the match with four first half goals after the Tigers jumped the Cats to lead by four goals at quarter time.
Tenacity and a series of undisciplined Richmond acts allowed the Cats back into the game and they dominated the last half with nine of the last 11 goals as the Tigers self- destructed.
Brownlow Medallist and co-captain Michael Voss returned to his best form helping Brisbane to a 31 point win over Adelaide at the Gabba on Friday night.
Voss had 38 possessions as Brisbane crept to fifth on the ladder joining Adelaide on nine wins and just two games from top spot.
Adelaide coach Malcolm Blight foreshadowed changes in the Crows' line-up as they prepare to play their next five games at home.
Coleman Medal favorite Tony Modra booted six goals for the Crows taking his season tally to 69 and streching his lead on the goal kicking table to 17.
SWITCHED ON POWER THRASHES MAGPIES
Port Adelaide dominated Collingwood from the outset to win by 57 points at Football Park on Saturday night, a 136 point turn around on their first meeting at the MCG in the opening round.
Led by inspirational skipper Gavin Wanganeen, the Power booted 10 straight goals before scoring a behind and need to win only three of their last six games to make the finals in their debut season.
Collingwood led the competition after round eight but now looks certain to miss the finals after losing seven of its past eight matches.
North Melbourne moved into the top eight and posted its first win since the return of skipper Wayne Carey three weeks ago with a 56 point win over Melbourne at the MCG on Sunday.

Melbourne's profligacy in front of goal where it kicked 7.16 for the day, cost it any chance of victory and was a source of frustration for caretaker coach Greg Hutchison following the Demons' stirring win over Carlton the week before.
*Andrew Bartram writes a regular AFL column for Reuters. Any feedback to michael.stapleton@reuters.com
